topic: Mental Capacity - I do not agree with the appointment or proposed appointment of someone's Donee. What can I do?
user_query: I do not agree with the appointment or proposed appointment of someone's Donee. What can I do?
variations: How can I object to the appointment of a Donee?
I am concerned about a Donee who has been appointed.
How can I stop someone from being appointed as Donee?
My family member chose this person to manage decisions but I do not trust him. Can this be changed?
part_a_general_info: A Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) is a legal document where an individual, known as a Donor, appoints one or more Donees to make decisions if the Donor loses mental capacity in future. An LPA can cover (a) Personal Welfare (for example, healthcare and daily care decisions) and/or (b) Property and Affairs (for example, bank accounts, bills, and property). The Donor must have mental capacity when making the LPA, and the LPA must be certified by an approved Certificate Issuer (such as an accredited doctor, psychiatrist, or lawyer). Donees can be appointed to act jointly or jointly and severally. PBSG cannot make, certify, or witness LPAs, but can share self-help resources, suggest next steps, and where appropriate route for legal-clinic intake.
triage_questions: Q1: Has the Donee already been appointed? (Answer options: Yes / No)
Q1A (ask if Q1=Yes): Has the Donor lost mental capacity? (Answer options: Yes / No / Not sure)

Q1B (ask if Q1A=Not sure): Any indicator of likely loss of capacity? (doctor said unable to decide, advised to consider deputyship, unconscious, cannot communicate, cannot understand/retain/use information) (Answer options: Yes / No / Not sure)
branching_logic: If Q1=Yes and Q1A=Yes: Route A.
If Q1=Yes and Q1A=No: Route C.
If Q1=Yes and Q1A=Not sure and Q1B=Yes: Route A.
If Q1=Yes and Q1A=Not sure and (Q1B=No or Not sure): Route C.
routing: Route A (Legal Clinics Process): explain legal-clinic scope, assess eligibility, send clinic application / appointment workflow, and share self-help resources.
Route B (Reject - resource-first): send OPG resources and explain applicant may re-contact PBSG if legal help is still needed after review.
Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff): gather more facts, take contact details, and escalate for staff follow-up.

routes.label: Legal Clinics Process
actions: Send clinic application or appointment workflow

routes.label: Reject - Resource First
actions: Explain re-contact channels if legal help is still needed

questions.prompt: Has the Donee already been appointed?
Has the Donor lost mental capacity?
Any indicator of likely loss of capacity (for example: doctor said unable to decide, advised to consider deputyship, unconscious, unable to communicate, unable to understand/retain/use information)?

guardrail: Must NOT assess mental capacity, assess conduct, or opine on whether a specific person should/should not be appointed Donee.
